name: Hydroxytyrosol (olive polyphenol)
short: Evidence is thin: one small trial (52 adults, 16 weeks) saw no adverse events; two others (1 week; 6 months, 29 women) only called it well tolerated. A review says long-term toxicity needs study.
text: Human safety data come from a few small randomised placebo-controlled trials of hydroxytyrosol capsules or supplements. In 52 adults aged 40-70 with overweight and prediabetes given hydroxytyrosol daily for 16 weeks (49 completed), no adverse events were observed. In 29 women with overweight or obesity given one of two daily amounts or placebo for six months, hydroxytyrosol was described as safe and well tolerated, and a one-week randomised trial of two daily amounts with a Latin square design also described it as well tolerated; these abstracts do not list specific adverse events. A toxicological evaluation of pure hydroxytyrosol proposed a no-observed-adverse-effect level of 500 mg/kg a day; the abstract does not describe the species, route, duration or design of the testing. A 2025 review concluded from animal and human studies that hydroxytyrosol shows low toxicity at physiologically relevant doses, but listed long-term toxicological outcomes as a direction for future research. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
